facts.citation: Same JSSC 52(1), 2017 as eyeriss_like.  Differs from it in ONE block: the 8 kB filter allocation the paper describes -- "the remaining 8 kB (two banks of 512-b x 64-b SRAMs) of the GLB is allocated for filter weights to compensate for insufficient off-chip traffic bandwidth" -- is declared as a Timeloop storage level instead of !Nothing. Unlike eyeriss_v2_like_wglb, whose weight level is NOT in its paper, this level IS published; what is uncertain is whether a prefetch buffer should be modelled as a reuse level.  The pair BRACKETS that uncertainty: eyeriss_like is the upper bound on DRAM weight traffic (and so on the ECC saving), eyeriss_like_wglb the lower bound. Quote the pair, never one alone.
facts.label: Eyeriss v1 (+8kB filter GLB)

notes: published at 65nm, modelled at 45nm. Deliberate: a mixed-node comparison would report silicon as architecture.

interconnect: multicast_network_no_routers -- wire 0.12 pJ/b/mm (shared); PE_column: router 0 pJ, ingress 0.915206 pJ, hop from area; PE: router 0 pJ, ingress 0.915206 pJ, hop from area (archs/_shared/noc.yaml)

simba_like.accumulator_evidence: "Each chip has a peak performance of 4 tera-ops per second (TOPS) using 8-bit weights and activations and 24-bit accumulation." Verified 2026-09-06.  The design as shipped by timeloop-accelergy-exercises declares PEAccuBuffer datawidth 24 but mac.adder_width 16, i.e. accumulator STORAGE at 24b and accumulator ARITHMETIC at 16b; 24 is the published number and is used for both.
simba_like.citation: Precisions only: Y. S. Shao et al., "Simba: Scaling Deep-Learning Inference with Multi-Chip-Module-Based Architecture", MICRO-52, 2019. The buffer and PE geometry come from timeloop-accelergy-exercises' example_designs/simba_like, which reproduces no published table.
simba_like.deviation: The largest node deviation in the study: Simba is a 16nm design modelled at 45nm.  Recorded, not corrected -- correcting it would reintroduce the mixed-node confound this contract removes.
simba_like.geometry_not_published: Two checks, both from numbers this repo has verified.  (1) MAC COUNT. The design instantiates 16 PEs x 4 distributed buffers x 4 reg/mac = 256 MACs.  The paper's own headline -- "4 tera-ops per second (TOPS) using 8-bit weights and activations" -- needs ~1024 MACs at Simba's published clock (2 ops per MAC, ~1.8 GHz), so this is a quarter-scale chiplet.  (2) BUFFER HIERARCHY.  As declared it has 1 MB of per-PE input buffer (64 kB x 16) and 2 MB of per-PE weight buffer (32 kB x 64) sitting behind a 64 kB shared GlobalBuffer -- 3 MB of private storage behind a shared buffer 48x smaller, which inverts the hierarchy.  The 2,113,536 on-chip weights that follow are 28x eyeriss_like's 75,264 and are what set this design's 1.4x DRAM refetch, hence its ECC saving. The MICRO-52 PDF could not be retrieved to correct the geometry (ACM and CACM paywalled, the Berkeley mirror 302s to a dead host), so the design is RELABELLED rather than silently re-dimensioned.
simba_like.label: Simba-like (reference design)

simple_input_stationary.accumulator_evidence: Matched to its two sibling reference dataflows so that the three simple designs differ only in which operand is stationary.
simple_input_stationary.citation: Authored in this repository, 2026-09-06.  timeloop-accelergy-exercises ships no input-stationary design and no paper is being reproduced. Built as the exact mirror of simple_weight_stationary and simple_output_stationary -- same mesh, same buffer capacities, same word widths -- with the PE scratchpad holding Inputs instead of Weights or Outputs, per section 9 of 01_project_context_and_architectures.txt. DIVERGED 2026-09-13 IN ONE BLOCK, and only in how the operand half is PARTITIONED: simple_weight_stationary's 64 kB operand_glb is now input_glb (28 kB) + weight_glb (36 kB), because a level holding Weights beside Inputs cannot declare the reconstruction arm's q-bit weights. This design and simple_output_stationary keep the single shared operand_glb. Total capacity, mesh and word widths are still identical; the level SET on the weight-stationary sibling is not.
simple_input_stationary.label: Input stationary

simple_output_stationary.accumulator_evidence: the design's own mac.adder_width; not published

simple_weight_stationary.accumulator_evidence: The design's own mac.adder_width. Not a published number -- it is the reference design's declaration, kept because changing it would be inventing a design point.
simple_weight_stationary.citation: Textbook weight-stationary reference shipped with timeloop-accelergy-exercises.  No paper; there is nothing to reproduce and nothing to cite beyond the exercises repo.
